markdown_report:
The best first step is a padding-aware temporal diagnostic for the supplied GRU4Rec. At 0% progress, verify recurrent execution before interpreting history sensitivity. Training-prefix results measure in-sample dependence, not generalization.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Feedback distinguishes broad relatedness from current usefulness. Histories cannot establish compatibility, redundancy, or mood; these remain hypotheses.
2. Existing embedding and margin probes do not establish held-out ranking quality. Perturbation effects likewise cannot separate useful memory from memorization.
3. Correct final-position readout is necessary but insufficient. Zero-input GRU steps can alter state through gates and biases; output masking cannot repair this.

**Insights from related work**

1. [Sampling reliability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) and [sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) motivate fixed candidates. Official 99-negative validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion.
2. [CETD](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/20/11176) motivates temporal counterfactuals. Synthetic deletions introduce distribution shifts, limiting attribution.
3. [Enhanced BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) highlights false negatives. Unobserved alternatives are comparison candidates, not verified dislikes.

**Directions and framework**

| Direction | Observable evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Interface correctness | Padding invariance, valid-position readout | Correctness does not establish relevance |
| Temporal dependence | Paired rank and state changes | Dependence does not establish utility |
| Candidate difficulty | Frequency-stratified margins | Frequency does not measure exposure |

**Candidate ideas**

Scores use 0–10; higher difficulty means greater implementation effort.

| Idea | Originality: positive / negative | Potential: positive / negative | Difficulty: positive / negative |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paired temporal probe | 4: connects states and ranks / familiar interventions | 7: guides experiments / in-sample attribution | 5: reuses hooks / padding and statistical checks |
| Frequency-stratified margin audit | 3: contextualizes margins / established slicing | 6: exposes uneven separation / limited generalization evidence | 2: reuses hooks / sparse slices |
| Jointly trained recency gate inside GRU | 4: adapts retention / overlaps GRU gating | 7: plausible adaptation / usefulness unverified | 5: compact layer / training and predictor updates |

**Selected algorithm: paired temporal utility probe**

Retain the probe, interpreting “utility” narrowly as conditional ranking sensitivity. First verify leading-padding invariance and batched-versus-unpadded agreement. If execution fails, correct recurrent padding and retrain consistently before interpretation; never silently alter checkpoint semantics ([PyTorch packing](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html)).

Sample one training prefix/target per eligible user; truncate once. Compare intact, equal-count recent/older/random deletion, final-preserving local shuffle, separate final-item removal, and last-item-only histories through the same checkpoint. Never refill deletions. Cache target plus 99 unique negatives using original exclusions, preserve legitimate repeated targets, and break score ties by item ID.

Report paired rank/HR@10 changes, state distances, repeat/novel slices, exclusions, and equal-category macro effects. Bootstrap users within category; intervals require 30 users/category/slice and remain conditional on checkpoints and candidates. Five simulator users/category support descriptive results only.

Preserve both diagnostic APIs, existing probes, empty unavailable-category breakdowns, and null missing measurements. Keep four single-model routes and official evaluation unchanged. No improvement or causal intent claim follows from this diagnostic.

idea.description: Strengthen the paired temporal utility probe with recurrent-padding verification, reproducible interventions, fixed candidates, and category-stratified uncertainty. Interpret its results as conditional in-sample temporal sensitivity rather than evidence of generalization or causal user intent.
idea.motivation: The feedback suggests weak alignment with recent intent, but existing training margins cannot establish whether temporal context changes rankings. At 0% progress, this diagnostic remains preferable to adding a recency gate before establishing padding correctness and measurable context dependence. Lower future-potential and higher implementation-difficulty ratings reflect the limits of in-sample evidence and the additional correctness work.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Retain embedding-collapse and sampled-margin probes. Access the actual trained module through view.model and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Category metadata is unavailable, so category-metadata breakdown lists remain empty; dataset-category routing is available and distinct. Do not infer ratings, review text, exposure, compatibility, mood, or simulator traits.

Preserve the corrected GRU4Rec family, one independently trained checkpoint per dataset category, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Do not inspect other trials or test files. This proposal normally requires no training or predictor changes. If padding verification exposes a defect, correcting execution changes model semantics: retrain the affected category models under the corrected architecture and update the embedded predictor writer and loader together. Never repair only diagnostic execution while reporting it as the original checkpoint's behavior.

Run under torch.inference_mode() with view.model.eval(); save and restore its previous training mode. A zero padding embedding does not make GRU recurrence inert. For packed execution, copy each sequence's valid items in chronological order to a right-padded temporary tensor; pack positive CPU lengths with enforce_sorted=False, execute the GRU, unpack and scatter outputs to the original valid positions. Handle empty histories separately without packing zero lengths. An alternative is a masked GRUCell update at every layer, retaining the previous hidden state when the input position is padding and emitting zero padding features. Packed execution generally avoids a Python timestep loop; use the host's corrected implementation unless a verified defect requires a change.

Before behavioral interpretation, compare aligned valid features, final features and candidate scores for individual unpadded histories versus batched left-padded execution, including singleton and empty histories. Test added leading zeros within supported input lengths. For float32 checks use atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4; record maximum discrepancies and numerical dtype. If comparing packed and masked implementations, copy identical weights and disable dropout. Gather final features using the maximum index with a nonzero item ID, never count minus one; for a nonempty strictly left-padded sequence this is L-1. Empty histories return zero sequence features and are excluded from prefix-target sensitivity examples; preserve any trained score bias consistently.

Verify per-position scoring for F[B,L,H] and item IDs I[B,L,K]: apply any trained output projection, multiply F.unsqueeze(-2) by the corresponding item embeddings, reduce over the embedding dimension, and include trained item biases. Require output shape B×L×K. Explicitly broadcast shared candidate lists and compare vectorized scoring with a small loop reference. Use the same scoring equations in diagnosis and prediction.

Use a dedicated diagnostic RNG seeded 42. Prespecify a maximum of 200 users per dataset category, sampled uniformly without replacement from eligible training users in sorted user-ID order. For each user, sample one target index uniformly from indices with at least five preceding training interactions; construct its preceding history and truncate it once to the model's existing maximum input length. Require at least five valid items after truncation for the complete intervention panel. Record eligible counts, sampled counts and exclusion reasons; audit unique (category, user, target-index) keys. These targets may already have participated in training, so label all outcomes in-sample sensitivity diagnostics. Do not change official input splits or use validation targets for this probe.

For a retained window of length n, set deletion count k=max(1,floor((n-1)/4)). Preserve the original final item for oldest-first, recent-first and random deletion: remove the first k, last k, or k uniformly selected positions among the first n-1 positions, respectively. Preserve chronological survivor order. Repeat random deletion five times. For local shuffling, partition the first n-1 positions into consecutive blocks of size three, independently permute positions inside each block, and repeat five times; the final item stays fixed. Include separate final-item removal and last-item-only conditions, plus an unchanged-input pass through the same transformation/scoring path. Repack and left-pad every condition to the same original model window. Never refill deleted positions from older interactions. Average repeated random-condition scalar effects within user before aggregation. Local shuffling measures sensitivity to altered order and may introduce implausible chronology; it does not isolate intent.

Cache one target plus 99 unique negative IDs per example, using the benchmark's original history-exclusion rule evaluated before perturbation. Exclude the target from negatives but retain legitimate earlier target occurrences in the input. Freeze candidate eligibility and candidate IDs across all conditions. If fewer than 99 eligible negatives exist, exclude the example and report the reason. Rank by descending score and then ascending item ID; do not favor targets in ties. Report repeat-target and novel-target slices separately. Match the benchmark's exclusion semantics without changing its evaluator; diagnostic RNG draws and candidates remain separate from official evaluation.

Define rank change as perturbed rank minus intact rank, so positive values mean worse ranking. Define HR@10 change as perturbed hit minus intact hit, so negative values mean worse ranking. Report final-state cosine distance and normalized displacement ||h_perturbed-h_intact||_2 / max(||h_intact||_2,1e-8); mark cosine distance unavailable when either norm is below 1e-8. State movement without rank damage establishes representation sensitivity only. Also report intact diagnostic HR@10, history-length slices 5–9, 10–19 and at least 20, and repeat/novel counts. Frequency-stratified margins use training item counts as a frequency proxy, never exposure.

For each condition, compute one paired scalar effect per user. Average within each dataset category, then give the four categories equal weight. Use 2,000 CPU bootstrap replicates with a separate RNG seeded 42, resampling users independently with replacement within each category, preserving paired outcomes and original category sample sizes; report percentile 2.5th–97.5th intervals. Require at least 30 unique users in every category contributing to a reported four-category interval or slice interval. Below that operational threshold, report descriptive category results and mark the corresponding four-category interval unavailable; if a category is absent, mark the four-category point estimate unavailable as well. Label any available-category summary separately. Flag constant effects and sparse slices. The five simulator users per category are a separate descriptive population and cannot supply these intervals.

Bound GPU work with the equal user cap, batches of at most 64 examples and candidate chunks of at most 100 IDs. Cache paired scalar outcomes and bootstrap on CPU without model refitting. Report inference time because diagnostics consume the shared search budget. Preserve required full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty simulator users separately. Intervals describe user sampling conditional on fitted checkpoints, selected prefixes and candidates; they omit seed variability, new-category generalization and validation-search selection optimism. Missing measurements return null plus reasons. Every metric definition must specify population, intervention, candidate construction, sign convention, denominator and counts. The interpreter prompt must distinguish measured effects from alternative explanations, including memorization, distribution shift, redundant histories and scoring bottlenecks. Official macro validation HR@10 alone selects models; no improvement is claimed before host measurement.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    preserve existing embedding and sampled-margin probes
    save model mode
    try:
        set view.model.eval(); enter inference_mode
        verify padding invariance, singleton/empty handling, and score shapes
        if correctness checks fail:
            return existing metrics plus failed checks and unavailable temporal metrics
        rng = RNG(42)
        for each of the four dataset categories:
            enumerate eligible training users deterministically
            sample at most 200 users without replacement
            for each user:
                sample one eligible training target index
                window = truncate preceding training history once
                cache target + 99 unique negatives using ORIGINAL exclusions
                if candidates insufficient: record exclusion; continue
                k = max(1, floor((len(window)-1)/4))
                variants = unchanged, oldest_delete(k), recent_delete(k),
                           random_delete(k, repeats=5),
                           block_shuffle(size=3, repeats=5),
                           final_item_remove, last_item_only
                preserve final item except in the explicitly separate removal condition
                for variant in variants:
                    preserve survivor chronology where applicable; never refill
                    left-pad to original model window
                    F = view.log2feats(sequence)
                    j = max index where sequence[j] != 0
                    state = F[j]
                    scores = view.predict_score(state, cached_candidates)
                    rank target by (-score, item_id)
                    record rank, hit_at_10, cosine distance and normalized displacement
                compute paired effects versus unchanged input
                average repeated-condition effects within user
                cache scalar outcomes, repeat/novel status and history-length slice
        aggregate category means and equal-weight four-category means
        bootstrap users within category 2000 times on CPU, seed=42
        enforce interval eligibility and report exclusions/constant effects
    finally:
        restore previous model mode
    return {metrics: results, metric_definitions: explicit_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics, definitions, counts and correctness-check results
    request evidence-linked findings, missing evidence and alternative explanations
    label training-prefix effects as in-sample conditional sensitivity
    prohibit inferred current intent, exposure, compatibility, dislikes or validation gains

originality.positive: Connects recurrent-state displacement, controlled temporal interventions, and paired ranking effects through the required GRU4Rec interface.
originality.negative: Padding checks, history perturbations, candidate controls, and paired bootstrap estimation are established methods; the contribution is their careful integration.

future_potential.positive: Can identify execution defects and distinguish state sensitivity from ranking sensitivity, supporting a focused subsequent recurrent-memory experiment.
future_potential.negative: In-sample interventions cannot separate useful memory from memorization, establish user intent, or predict official validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing model hooks and checkpoints, with bounded inference and CPU-only resampling.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducibility requires padding verification, scoring-shape tests, candidate exclusions, repeated interventions, sparse-slice handling, and potentially consistent retraining if execution is defective.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: Examines ranking-sampler reliability across resolution, fidelity, exposure bias, and recovery of preference rankings.
Supports explicitly separating diagnostic candidate results from the pinned benchmark.
limitations: Does not establish that diagnostic candidate rankings predict RecHarness validation performance.

related_work.title: CETD
contributions: Provides methodological motivation for temporally structured counterfactual histories.
limitations: Does not validate these GRU4Rec probes or establish deletion sensitivity as evidence of stale or useful memory.

related_work.title: Enhanced Bayesian Personalized Ranking
contributions: Addresses false negatives as a source of misleading recommendation training signals.
limitations: Does not reveal whether individual unobserved diagnostic candidates are relevant or disliked.

related_work.title: GRU4Rec reference implementation
contributions: Provides the recurrent recommendation family underlying the required baseline.
limitations: Session-oriented behavior does not establish correct left-padding and whole-history execution in the host implementation.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent gates and biases, explaining why zero input does not guarantee an unchanged hidden state.
limitations: Documents execution semantics rather than recommendation quality or the host model's correctness.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence documentation
contributions: Documents packed variable-length execution, CPU tensor lengths, and enforce_sorted=False.
limitations: Left-padded inputs require chronological compaction before packing and output scattering afterward; empty histories need separate handling.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes limitations of recommendation metrics computed with sampled candidates.
limitations: Does not make a fixed sampled diagnostic equivalent to full-catalog ranking.

related_work.title: Data Leakage in Offline Evaluation
contributions: Motivates careful separation of training information and offline evaluation.
limitations: Does not convert training-prefix sensitivity into evidence of temporal generalization.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling principles for preserving correspondence between observations.
limitations: The four-category macro estimand requires explicit within-category resampling; ordinary pooled resampling is insufficient.
The proposed 30-user reporting rule is an operational choice, not a guarantee of interval coverage.

related_work.title: R boot documentation
limitations: Resampling users conditional on a fitted checkpoint does not capture training-seed or candidate-sampling variability.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how model-selection procedures can overfit evaluation criteria and bias reported performance.
limitations: Ordinary diagnostic bootstrap intervals do not correct repeated validation-guided selection or supply a task-specific correction.
